bib.title: MAmmoTH2: Scaling Instructions from the Web
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v4, 23 May 2024); the note cites NeurIPS 2024, which the PDF does not print

question: Can large-scale, high-quality reasoning instruction data be mined from the pre-training web corpus instead of human annotation or GPT-4 distillation?
hypothesis: Web corpora already contain diverse, high-quality instruction-response pairs that can be recalled, extracted and refined to improve reasoning generalisation.
contributions: WebInstruct: 10M instruction-response pairs mined via recall, extract, refine
MAmmoTH2 models trained on WebInstruct, large held-out reasoning gains
MAmmoTH2-Plus after further tuning on public datasets, strong reasoning and chat results

method.summary: Three-step pipeline: fastText recall of 18M Common Crawl docs, Qwen-72B extraction of ~5M Q-A pairs, refinement by Mixtral-8x22B and Qwen-72B into 10M pairs. Base models are SFT'd on it (WebInstruct), then optionally on public sets (Plus).

datasets.name: WebInstruct
datasets.size: 10M Q-A pairs, ~5B tokens (from 18M recalled documents, ~5M extracted candidates)
datasets.source: Common Crawl (internal CC, RedPajama cited); recalled by fastText, extracted by Qwen-72B, refined by Mixtral-8x22B and Qwen-72B
datasets.preprocessing: HTML rule-based cleaning; 10-gram string match decontamination against all eval questions/answers; only domains with >1000 docs retained; ~600K domains, ~50K labelled positive by GPT-3.5

datasets.name: fastText seed set
datasets.size: 100K positive (crawled quiz/exam sites) + 100K random negative CC docs
datasets.preprocessing: fastText dim 256, 3 epochs, lr 0.1, max n-gram 3, max word occurrences 3; round 2 retrained on documents from GPT-3.5-selected domains vs rest

datasets.name: Math-Plus
datasets.source: MetaMathQA 395K + Orca-Math 200K + 300K GPT-4 rewrites of MATH train

other.Plus: WebInstruct first, then continued on additional public datasets

training.objective: SFT loss (multi-turn instruction format); ablation compares LM loss
training.lr: 5e-6 for Mistral 7B; 1e-5 for Mixtral, Llama-3 8B, Yi 34B
training.steps: 9000 steps in the Table 4 refiner ablation; main run not stated

other.Plus training: first WebInstruct, then continue on public datasets (Appendix E); hyperparameters for the second stage not stated

inference.prompting: few-shot CoT: TheoremQA 5-shot, MATH 4-shot, GSM8K 4-shot, GPQA 5-shot, MMLU-STEM 5-shot, BBH 3-shot, ARC-C 8-shot

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: per benchmark few-shot CoT accuracy; AVG is mean of seven

metrics.name: MT-Bench, AlpacaEval 2.0, Arena Hard, MMLU, MMLU-Pro

eval.protocol: Single runs, no seeds or significance tests stated; baseline numbers taken from papers/leaderboards when available, else own script; human check on 50 refined samples

evidence.where: Sec 2.3; printed as 22B×8 though Mixtral is 8x7B in Sec 1 and elsewhere

results.claim: MAmmoTH2-7B (Mistral) raises MATH from 11% to 36.7% with WebInstruct only
results.setup: Mistral-7B base fine-tuned on WebInstruct only (10M pairs), 2 epochs, few-shot CoT eval (MATH 4-shot, GSM8K 4-shot); no benchmark training data, 10-gram decontamination
results.quote: Notably, Mistral-7B’s MATH accuracy can rise from 11.2% to 36.7% after training on WEBINSTRUCT.

results.setup: Mistral-7B base fine-tuned on WebInstruct only (10M pairs), 2 epochs, few-shot CoT eval (MATH 4-shot, GSM8K 4-shot); no benchmark training data, 10-gram decontamination
results.note: Abstract prints 36%; Table 2 base Mistral-7B is 36.2.
results.quote: from 11% to 36.7% on MATH and from 36% to 68.4% on GSM8K without training

results.claim: Average gain over base on seven reasoning benchmarks, 7B
results.setup: MAmmoTH2-7B vs Mistral-7B, WebInstruct only; TheoremQA, MATH, GSM8K, GPQA, MMLU-STEM, BBH, ARC-C
results.quote: MAmmoTH2-7B boosts the performance of Mistral-7B by an average of 14 points.

results.setup: Yi-34B base, WebInstruct only, same seven benchmarks
results.quote: MAmmoTH2-34B enhances Yi-34B’s performance by an average of 5.8 absolute points.
MAmmoTH2-8B boosts the performance of Llama-3-8B-base by an average of 8.8 points.

results.setup: Llama-3-8B base; WebInstruct then additional public datasets; Llama-3-Instruct trained on 10M human-annotated data plus public data
results.note: Table 2 averages: 59.1 vs 53.4 (5.7); intro says 6 points.
results.quote: MAmmoTH2-8B-Plus outperforms Llama3-Instruct by an average of 6% across the benchmarks.

results.claim: MAmmoTH2-8x7B-Plus about matches Qwen-1.5-110B with 13B active parameters
results.quote: MAmmoTH2-8x7B-Plus can even match the performance of Qwen-1.5-110B with only 13B active parameters.

results.claim: Q-A extraction keeps only 30% of recalled documents
results.metric: fraction of docs with Q-A pairs
results.setup: 18M recalled docs, Qwen-72B extractor with in-context examples
results.quote: only 30% of the recalled documents were identified as containing naturally existing Q-A pairs, resulting in roughly 5M Q-A pairs

results.claim: Human check of 50 refined examples: improved vs hallucinated
results.setup: 50 randomly sampled refined QA examples, human annotators
results.quote: 78% examples have been improved after refinement and only 10% examples introduce hallucinations after refinement.

results.claim: Merged (Mixtral+Qwen) refinement vs single refiner, GSM8K
results.setup: Mistral-7B, 9000 steps, global batch 512; Mixtral 62.9, Qwen 65.4
results.note: Merged does not win everywhere: TheoremQA Mixtral 26.1 vs merged 24.8; MMLU-S Qwen 60.6 vs merged 60.5.

results.claim: Education sources beat forum sources on GSM8K
results.setup: Mistral-7B trained on subsets by source; forum 51.0; base 47.4
results.note: MMLU-S forum 54.7 vs education 54.3, so not uniform despite 'consistently'.

results.claim: Math-domain subset helps MATH most but not GSM8K or science
results.setup: Mistral-7B trained on math subset; GSM8K 52.9, ARC-C 74.1 (base 77.6)
Labels from Llama-3-8B-Instruct; math 68.36% within science
results.quote: 81.69% of the data falling under the broad "Science" category

results.claim: WebInstruct source split, exam-style vs forum
results.quote: the vast majority (86.73%) of the instruction-response pairs come from exam-style questions, while forum discussions make up the remaining 13.27%

results.claim: SFT loss beats LM loss and accuracy rises with more instructions (1M to 10M)
results.setup: Mistral-7B, MATH/TheoremQA/ARC-C, read from Fig 5; no numbers in text

limits: Noise and inaccuracies remain; extraction and refinement depend on the LLMs used (App H)
Humanities and daily-chat topics underrepresented (App H)
Single runs, no seeds, variance not reported
Baseline numbers mix official sources and own evaluation, so settings differ
Raw documents lacking CoT rationale; refinement can change intent (10% hallucinations in 50-sample check)
Intro says Mixtral extracts Q-A pairs, Sec 2.2 says Qwen-72B; refiner printed as Mixtral-22Bx8 / Mixtral-8x7B inconsistently
First-round recalled docs are discarded; GPT-3.5/GPT-4 are used to select domains, so pipeline is not GPT-free
